Grid.succ.statement: Let $X$ be a pseudometric space equipped with the standing Carleson data $\mathrm{ProofData}(a, q, K, \sigma_1, \sigma_2, F, G)$ (with $a \in \mathbb{N}$, $q \in \mathbb{R}$, a kernel $K : X \times X \to \mathbb{C}$, functions $\sigma_1, \sigma_2 : X \to \mathbb{Z}$ and sets $F, G \subseteq X$), and with a grid structure $\mathrm{GridStructure}(X, \mathrm{defaultD}(a), \mathrm{default}\kappa(a), \mathrm{defaultS}(X), \mathrm{cancelPt}(X))$. Definition: for a dyadic cube $i \in \mathrm{Grid}(X)$, a cube $\mathrm{succ}(i) \in \mathrm{Grid}(X)$. According to the docstring, if $i$ is not a maximal element, this is the (unique) minimal element greater than $i$; and this does not form a successor order, since an element can be the successor of multiple other elements.
